blurb.en: The long-hand way to build a new list: start empty, loop, and add one item per pass.
blurb.zh: 造新列表的「手写版」：先空着，循环一遍，每轮往里加一项。

en: Building a new list from an old one always takes the same three steps: make an empty list, go through the old items one at a time, and add the new item you work out from each. This program is that pattern with nothing else in the way, so it is worth being able to write without thinking.
append changes the list it is called on and gives back None, so it is used as a statement on its own line. Writing result = result.append(...) would throw the list away and leave result holding None.

The function accepts anything a for loop can walk through, not only lists: the third call passes range(4) and still gets a list back, because result is always a list. The program "Squares: List Comprehension" builds exactly the same list in one line.
zh: 由旧列表造新列表，永远是同样三步：先建一个空列表，逐个看旧列表的每一项，把由它算出的新项加进去。这个程序就是这个模式本身、别无他物，值得练到不假思索就能写出来。
append 直接改动调用它的那个列表，交回的是 None，所以它单独占一行当语句用。写成 result = result.append(...) 会把列表丢掉，让 result 变成 None。
这个函数接受任何 for 能遍历的东西，不只是列表：第三次调用传的是 range(4)，拿回来的照样是列表，因为 result 始终是列表。「平方表：列表推导式」这个程序用一行造出一模一样的列表。

lineNotes.en: Only reached after the loop has finished, so every square is already in the list. Indented one level further, inside the loop, it would return after the first item.
lineNotes.zh: 循环整个跑完才走到这里，所有平方都已经在列表里了。要是多缩进一层、放进循环里，加完第一项就 return 了。

blurb.en: The same list of squares in one line - an empty list, a loop and append, folded into brackets.
blurb.zh: 同一张平方表写成一行——空列表、循环、append 三样折进一对方括号。

en: A list comprehension has the shape [expression for item in iterable]. Read it as: for each item in the iterable, work out the expression, and collect the results in a new list. It does the same job as the loop-and-append version and gives an identical result for every input - compare the two programs side by side.

The expression comes first even though it is worked out last. That order is the part that feels backwards at first: the brackets say what each new item looks like before they say where the items come from.

The loop variable belongs to the comprehension. It does not exist before it, and in Python 3 it does not survive after it, so a comprehension cannot accidentally overwrite a variable of the same name outside.

Use a comprehension when the job is exactly build a new list from an old one. When the loop body has to do more than produce one value per item, the plain loop is the better tool - the program "Comprehension or Loop?" is about that.
zh: 列表推导式的形状是 [表达式 for 项 in 可迭代对象]。读法：对可迭代对象里的每一项，算出表达式，把结果收进一个新列表。它和「循环加 append」那个版本做的是同一件事，对任何输入结果都相同——把两个程序并排对照看看。
表达式写在最前面，虽然它是最后才算的。一开始觉得别扭的就是这个顺序：方括号先说「每个新项长什么样」，再说「项从哪里来」。
循环变量属于推导式自己。推导式之前它不存在，在 Python 3 里推导式结束后它也不留下，所以推导式不会意外覆盖外面同名的变量。
当任务恰好是「由旧列表造新列表」时用推导式。循环体要做的事不止「每项产出一个值」时，普通循环才是合适的工具——「推导式还是循环？」这个程序讲的就是这个。

title.en: Keep the Evens: Comprehension with if
title.zh: 只留偶数：带 if 的推导式

blurb.en: An if at the end of a comprehension decides which items make it into the new list.
blurb.zh: 推导式末尾的 if 决定哪些项能进新列表。

en: Adding if condition after the for turns a comprehension into a filter: an item is kept only when the condition is true for it, and the items that are kept go in unchanged. The new list can be shorter than the old one, or empty, as the second call shows.
Even means the remainder after dividing by 2 is 0. That works for negative numbers and zero too: in Python -4 % 2 is 0 and 0 % 2 is 0, so both are kept.
The filtered comprehension does the same job as a loop with an if inside and one append under it. The paired program does it a third way, with the built-in filter.
zh: 在 for 后面加上 if 条件，推导式就成了筛子：只有条件为真的项才留下，留下的项原样放进去。新列表可以比旧的短，也可以是空的，第二次调用就是这样。
偶数的意思是除以 2 的余数为 0。这对负数和 0 同样成立：Python 里 -4 % 2 是 0，0 % 2 也是 0，所以两个都留下。
带筛选的推导式和「循环里一个 if、if 下一个 append」做的是同一件事。配对的程序用第三种方式——内置的 filter——来做。

title.en: Keep the Evens: filter and lambda

blurb.en: Hand filter a yes-or-no function and it keeps the items that get a yes - lazily.
blurb.zh: 给 filter 一个回答「是或否」的函数，它就留下答「是」的项——而且是惰性的。

en: filter(function, iterable) calls the function on each item and keeps the items for which it returns something true. The function here is a lambda: a one-expression function written in place, so there is no need to def a named function used only once.

filter does not build a list. It hands back a filter object, an iterator that produces the kept items only when something asks for them, and it can be gone through only once. That is why the second line converts it before returning: printing the filter object itself would show something like <filter object at 0x...>, not the numbers.

Most Python programmers find the comprehension version easier to read than filter with a lambda, and it is the more common style. filter reads well when you already have a named function to pass, such as filter(str.isdigit, parts).
zh: filter(函数, 可迭代对象) 对每一项调用函数，留下返回真值的那些项。这里的函数是一个 lambda：就地写出来的单表达式函数，只用一次的函数不必专门 def 一个名字。
filter 不建列表。它交回一个 filter 对象——一个迭代器，有人来要时才一项项产出留下的值，而且只能走一遍。所以第二行先转换再 return：直接打印 filter 对象，看到的是 <filter object at 0x...> 这样的东西，不是那些数。
多数 Python 程序员觉得推导式版本比 filter 加 lambda 好读，它也是更常见的写法。手头已经有一个现成的具名函数时，filter 读起来才顺，比如 filter(str.isdigit, parts)。

blurb.en: Stop writing range(len(...)): enumerate numbers the items for you, and zip walks two lists in step.
blurb.zh: 别再写 range(len(...))：enumerate 替你编号，zip 让两个列表齐步走。

en: The loop for i in range(len(names)) followed by names[i] works, but it makes you manage an index you do not really want. enumerate(names) hands over (index, item) pairs, and the for unpacks each pair into two names. Counting normally starts at 0; passing start=1 makes it start where a ranking does.

zip(names, scores) pairs the first item of each list, then the second, and so on, which is the usual way to go through two related lists together. Passing the pairs to dict() makes a dictionary straight away, the first list giving the keys and the second the values.

zip stops as soon as the shorter input runs out, without an error: the last line pairs three names with two numbers and gets two pairs. That is convenient, but it can hide a bug where one list is shorter than it should be.
zh: for i in range(len(names)) 再配 names[i] 能用，但它让你去管一个你其实并不想要的下标。enumerate(names) 交出 (下标, 项) 二元组，for 把每一对拆进两个名字。计数通常从 0 开始；传 start=1 就从排名该有的 1 开始。
zip(names, scores) 把两个列表的第一项配成一对、再第二项，依此类推——这是同时遍历两个相关列表的惯用法。把这些对交给 dict()，当场就是一个字典：第一个列表出键，第二个出值。
只要较短的那个输入用完，zip 就停，不报错：最后一行把三个名字和两个数配对，只得到两对。这很方便，但也可能掩盖「某个列表比应有的短」这种 bug。

lineNotes.en: Three names, two numbers: zip quietly stops after two pairs, and Chen is simply left out.
lineNotes.zh: 三个名字、两个数：zip 配完两对就悄悄停下，Chen 直接被落下。

lineNotes.en: Once the lists are a dictionary, finding Chen's score is one lookup instead of a search through names for the right index.
lineNotes.zh: 两个列表一旦变成字典，查 Chen 的分数就是一次取值，不用先在 names 里找出下标。

run.expect:
1. Ada
2. Brian
3. Chen
Ada: 91
Brian: 64
Chen: 88
{'Ada': 91, 'Brian': 64, 'Chen': 88}
88
[('Ada', 1), ('Brian', 2)]

title.zh: 字典推导式与集合推导式

blurb.en: Curly braces with a colon build a dictionary; curly braces without one build a set.
blurb.zh: 花括号里带冒号造字典，不带冒号造集合。

en: A dictionary comprehension writes key: value where a list comprehension writes a single expression. Walking mapping.items() gives each key together with its value, so inverting a dictionary is a matter of writing the two the other way round.

Keys must be unique, so when two old keys share a value, the inverted dictionary can keep only one of them. The later one wins, because it is written in after the earlier one: in the second call both a and c map to 1, and 1 ends up pointing at c.
word_lengths shows the most common use: a lookup table built from a list in one line. Apple and apple are different strings, so both become keys.

A set comprehension looks like a list comprehension in curly braces. A set keeps each value only once, so five words starting with a, a, b, c and a give three letters. A set has no order you can rely on - it can come out differently each time the program runs, even on the same computer, because Python picks a new random seed for hashing strings every time it starts - so the program sorts it before printing.
zh: 字典推导式在列表推导式写单个表达式的位置写 键: 值。遍历 mapping.items() 能同时拿到每个键和它的值，所以反转字典就是把两者倒过来写。
键必须唯一，所以两个旧键的值相同时，反转后的字典只能留下其中一个。留下的是后来的那个，因为它是在前一个之后写进去的：第二次调用里 a 和 c 都对应 1，最后 1 指向的是 c。
word_lengths 是最常见的用法：一行由列表造出一张查询表。Apple 和 apple 是不同的字符串，所以两个都成了键。
集合推导式长得像写在花括号里的列表推导式。集合里每个值只留一份，所以首字母是 a、a、b、c、a 的五个词只得到三个字母。集合没有可依赖的顺序——同一台电脑上每次运行都可能不同（取决于字符串哈希随机化：Python 每次启动都给字符串哈希换一个随机种子）——所以程序先排序再打印。

lineNotes.en: sorted accepts a set and returns a list in order, so the output is the same on every run.
lineNotes.zh: sorted 接受集合、交回排好序的列表，所以每次运行的输出都一样。

title.zh: 嵌套推导式：展平与转置

blurb.en: Two fors in one pair of brackets flatten a grid; brackets inside brackets turn its rows into columns.
blurb.zh: 一对方括号里两个 for，把网格展平；方括号套方括号，把行变成列。

en: Flattening uses a single comprehension with two fors. They are written in the same order as the equivalent nested loops - the outer loop first, the inner loop second - so the rule is: write the loops as you would indent them, then move the item to the front. Writing the inner for first fails, because it would use row before row exists.

Transposing is different: the result is itself a list of lists, so there is a comprehension inside a comprehension. The outer one runs once per column number and produces one new row; the inner one, for that column number, takes the matching cell from every row. Reading it inside out helps: the inner brackets are one column.

The column numbers come from the length of the first row, which assumes every row is the same length and that there is at least one row. Transposing twice gets back the original grid, and a 3-by-2 grid becomes a 2-by-3 one, as the last line shows.
Two levels of nesting is about as far as a comprehension stays readable. Past that, the same work written as ordinary nested loops is easier to follow.
zh: 展平用的是一个推导式、两个 for。它们的先后与对应的两层循环相同——外层在前、内层在后——所以规则是：按缩进时的顺序写循环，再把项挪到最前面。把内层 for 写在前面会出错，因为那时 row 还不存在。
转置不一样：结果本身是列表的列表，所以是推导式里套推导式。外层对每个列号跑一次、产出一行新的；内层针对这个列号，从每一行取出对应的格子。从里往外读有帮助：内层方括号就是一列。
列号取自第一行的长度，这默认了每行一样长、并且至少有一行。转置两次回到原网格；3 行 2 列变成 2 行 3 列，最后一行演示的就是这个。
嵌套两层差不多是推导式还能保持好读的极限。再往深，写成普通的嵌套循环更容易看懂。

lineNotes.en: Rows can have different lengths for flattening, and an empty row simply contributes nothing.
lineNotes.zh: 展平时各行可以长短不一，空行就是什么都不贡献。

lineNotes.en: Swapping rows and columns twice puts everything back where it was.
lineNotes.zh: 行列对调两次，一切回到原位。

title.en: Generator Expressions with sum, any and all

blurb.en: Round brackets instead of square ones: the values are produced one at a time and no list is ever built.
blurb.zh: 方括号换成圆括号：值一个个产出，从头到尾不建列表。

en: A generator expression looks like a list comprehension in round brackets. Instead of building the whole list first, it produces one value each time it is asked. When it is the only argument of a function call, the call's own brackets are enough, which is why sum(... for ... in ...) needs no extra pair.

sum, any and all only need to see the values one at a time, so a generator is all they need. any stops at the first true value and all stops at the first false one, so on a long list they may not look at most of it.

Counting with sum is a common trick: add a 1 for every item that passes the if. Empty input is worth remembering: all of nothing is True (there is no item that fails), any of nothing is False, and the sum is 0 - the third call shows all three.
A generator can be used only once. Once sum has run through the squares, they are used up, and a second sum over the same generator finds nothing and gives 0. A list would give 14 both times.
zh: 生成器表达式长得像写在圆括号里的列表推导式。它不先把整个列表造出来，而是每被要一次产出一个值。当它是函数调用的唯一实参时，调用自己的圆括号就够了，所以 sum(... for ... in ...) 不必再套一层。
sum、any、all 只需要一个个地看值，所以给它们生成器就够了。any 遇到第一个真值就停，all 遇到第一个假值就停，长列表的大部分它们可能根本不看。
用 sum 计数是常见技巧：每个通过 if 的项加一个 1。空输入值得记住：空的 all 是 True（没有不合格的项），空的 any 是 False，sum 是 0——第三次调用把三样都演示了。
生成器只能用一次。sum 把平方跑完一遍，它们就用光了；对同一个生成器再 sum 一次什么都找不到，得到 0。换成列表，两次都是 14。

lineNotes.at: full_marks = any(mark == 100 for mark in marks)
lineNotes.en: any answers: is there at least one? It stops looking as soon as it finds a 100.
lineNotes.zh: any 回答的是：至少有一个吗？一找到 100 就不再往下看。

lineNotes.en: The first sum uses the generator up; the second finds it already empty.
lineNotes.zh: 第一个 sum 把生成器用光了；第二个拿到的已经是空的。

run.expect:
(4, False, True)
(2, True, False)
(0, True, False)
generator
14 0

title.en: Read Several Numbers from One Line

blurb.en: input() gives one string; split breaks it into pieces and map turns every piece into an int.
blurb.zh: input() 给的是一个字符串；split 把它切成几段，map 把每段都变成 int。

en: input() always returns one string, even when someone types several numbers. split() with no argument cuts it at any run of spaces and ignores spaces at either end, so '  6    7 ' becomes ['6', '7']. map(int, pieces) then calls int on every piece.

map, like filter, is lazy and hands back an iterator, so read_ints wraps it in list() to get a real list it can return. When you know exactly how many numbers are on the line, you can skip the list and unpack the map straight into names, as the width and height line does; the wrong count of numbers raises a ValueError.

Splitting on a comma instead is different: split(',') cuts at each comma exactly and keeps any spaces, so '1, 2,3' gives '1', ' 2' and '3'. The spaces do no harm here, because int ignores spaces around a number, and the last line converts the pieces with a comprehension.

To try it, type three lines: 3 14 15 92, then '  6    7 ' with extra spaces, then 1, 2,3. When those lines come from a file or a pipe instead - which is how the program is checked - input() does not echo them, so each prompt is followed directly by what the program prints next.
zh: input() 永远交回一个字符串，哪怕对方敲了好几个数。不带实参的 split() 在任意一段空白处切开，并忽略两端的空白，所以 '  6    7 ' 变成 ['6', '7']。然后 map(int, 各段) 对每一段调用 int。
map 和 filter 一样是惰性的、交回迭代器，所以 read_ints 用 list() 把它包起来，得到一个真正的列表再 return。确切知道一行有几个数时，可以不要列表、直接把 map 拆进几个名字，宽高那一行就是这样；数的个数不对会抛 ValueError。
按逗号切则不同：split(',') 严格在每个逗号处切开、保留空格，所以 '1, 2,3' 得到 '1'、' 2'、'3'。这些空格在这里无害，因为 int 会忽略数字两边的空格；最后一行用推导式来转换。
试一试：依次敲三行——3 14 15 92，然后是带多余空格的 '  6    7 '，然后是 1, 2,3。如果这几行是从文件或管道喂进去的（检查程序就是这样跑的），input() 不回显它们，每个提示后面就紧跟程序接着打印的东西。

lineNotes.en: With an argument, split cuts at exactly that text and nothing else, so the space after the first comma stays attached to the 2.
lineNotes.zh: 带实参的 split 只在那段文字处切，别处一概不切，所以第一个逗号后面的空格仍然粘在 2 前面。

run.expect:
Numbers: [3, 14, 15, 92] 124
Width and height: 42
Comma list: ['1', ' 2', '3']
[1, 2, 3]

title.en: sorted, min and max with key=

blurb.en: key= says what to compare; a tuple key breaks ties; and a stable sort never reorders equals.
blurb.zh: key= 指定拿什么来比；元组当 key 能分出平局；稳定排序从不打乱相等的项。

en: sorted, min and max compare whole items unless told otherwise. key= gives them a function to call on each item, and they compare what that function returns instead. The items themselves come back unchanged: sorting by score still returns (name, score) tuples.

Python's sort is stable: items whose keys are equal stay in the order they were in. Chen came before Bob in the list and both scored 88, so Chen is still before Bob after sorting by score. Stability is what lets you sort by one thing and trust the earlier order to settle ties.

A tuple key sorts by several things at once, because tuples are compared item by item. Negating the score puts high scores first while the names in the second item still go in ordinary alphabetical order - reverse=True would reverse the names too.

min and max take the same key=. When several items tie for the largest, max returns the first of them, so Ada rather than Dan. Without a key, max compares the tuples themselves, which means by name first - and Eve is the largest name, not the top score.
zh: sorted、min、max 默认比较整个项。key= 给它们一个函数，对每一项调用，它们改为比较这个函数的返回值。项本身原样交回：按分数排序，拿回来的仍是 (名字, 分数) 元组。
Python 的排序是稳定的：key 相等的项保持原来的先后。列表里 Chen 在 Bob 前面、两人都是 88 分，所以按分数排完 Chen 仍在 Bob 前面。正因为稳定，你才能按一样东西排序、并放心让原来的顺序去分出平局。
元组当 key 可以同时按好几样东西排，因为元组是逐项比较的。把分数取负让高分排在前面，而第二项的名字仍按普通字母序——用 reverse=True 的话名字也会跟着倒过来。
min 和 max 接受同样的 key=。好几项并列最大时，max 交回其中第一个，所以是 Ada 而不是 Dan。不给 key 时，max 比较元组本身，也就是先比名字——于是最大的是名字最靠后的 Eve，而不是分数最高的人。

lineNotes.en: The same key as by_score: compare by score, but hand back the whole tuple.
lineNotes.zh: 和 by_score 用同一个 key：按分数比，交回整个元组。

lineNotes.en: No key: tuples are compared by their first item, the name, so this finds the name latest in the alphabet.
lineNotes.zh: 没有 key：元组按第一项、也就是名字来比，所以找到的是字母序最靠后的名字。

title.en: Where the if Goes in a Comprehension
title.zh: 推导式里 if 放在哪

blurb.en: Before the for, an if-else changes every item; after the for, an if drops items.
blurb.zh: 放在 for 前面的 if-else 改写每一项；放在 for 后面的 if 筛掉项。

en: These two look alike and do different jobs. An if-else before the for is a conditional expression - value_if_true if condition else value_if_false - and it is part of the item: every item of the old list produces one item of the new one, so the length stays the same. An if after the for is a filter: items that fail are left out, so the new list can be shorter.
The third output line counts it: six readings, six clipped values, four kept values.

Mixing the two up gives a syntax error rather than a wrong answer. An if at the end cannot have an else, and an if before the for must have one, because every item needs a value. If Python complains about else in a comprehension, check which side of the for the if is on.
Both can appear in one comprehension - a conditional expression in front and a filter at the back - but at that point a plain loop is usually clearer.
zh: 这两种长得像，干的活却不同。for 前面的 if-else 是条件表达式——真时的值 if 条件 else 假时的值——它是「项」的一部分：旧列表每一项都产出新列表的一项，所以长度不变。for 后面的 if 是筛子：不满足的项被去掉，新列表可能更短。
输出第三行把这点数了出来：六个读数，裁剪后六个，筛选后四个。
把两种弄混得到的是语法错误，而不是错的答案。末尾的 if 不能带 else；for 前面的 if 必须带 else，因为每一项都得有个值。Python 抱怨推导式里的 else 时，先看看 if 在 for 的哪一边。
两种可以出现在同一个推导式里——前面条件表达式、后面筛子——但到了那一步，普通循环通常更清楚。

lineNotes.at: print(["even" if n % 2 == 0 else "odd" for n in range(4)])
lineNotes.en: A conditional expression can produce a different kind of value from the input: numbers go in, words come out, one per number.
lineNotes.zh: 条件表达式产出的值可以和输入不是一类：进去的是数，出来的是词，一个数一个词。

blurb.en: Two jobs a comprehension can do but should not: one done only for its side effect, and one with three loops deep.
blurb.zh: 推导式做得了、却不该做的两件事：只为副作用而做的，和嵌套三层的。

en: A comprehension exists to build a list. shout_all_comprehension uses one only to call print, so it builds a list nobody wants - the output shows [None, None], one None per call to print - and a reader expects a result that is never used. When the point of the loop is what it does, not what it makes, write a for loop.

rising_triples_comprehension fits on one line but asks the reader to hold three loops and a condition in mind at once. It is also written the most direct way: b and c each run over the whole of range(n), so for n = 4 it tries all 64 combinations and its if throws away all but 4.

The loop version starts each inner range just above the outer variable, so the a < b < c test is never needed and no combination is thrown away. That trick is not something only a loop can do: the same starting points fit inside a comprehension just as well, with no test and nothing wasted. The real reason to switch to a loop is reading it - with three fors squeezed onto one line it is hard to see which range belongs to which variable, while the loop version reads from top to bottom, one level at a time.

Both functions return the same list, as the last line checks. A reasonable rule of thumb: one for, or one for with an if, is a good comprehension; two fors is the limit; three, or anything with a side effect, is a loop.
zh: 推导式是用来造列表的。shout_all_comprehension 用它只是为了调用 print，于是造出一个没人要的列表——输出里的 [None, None]，每调一次 print 一个 None——读代码的人还会以为有个结果要用，其实从没用上。循环的意义在于它做了什么、而不在于它造出什么时，就写 for 循环。
rising_triples_comprehension 一行写得下，但要读的人同时在脑子里装下三层循环和一个条件。它还是照最直白的方式写的：b 和 c 都跑遍整个 range(n)，所以 n = 4 时试遍 64 种组合，再由它的 if 扔得只剩 4 种。
循环版本让每层内循环的 range 都从外层变量的下一个数开始，所以根本不需要 a < b < c 这个判断，也没有任何组合被扔掉。但这个技巧不是循环才有的：同样的起点写进推导式里也完全可以，一样不用判断、一个组合都不浪费。真正该换回循环的理由是好不好读——三个 for 挤在一行，哪个 range 属于哪个变量很难一眼看清；循环版本则从上往下、一层一层地读。
两个函数返回同一个列表，最后一行验证了这一点。一个合理的经验法则：一个 for，或一个 for 加一个 if，是好推导式；两个 for 是上限；三个，或者带副作用的，写成循环。

lineNotes.en: c starts just above b for the same reason b starts just above a: the combinations that would fail the test are never produced.
lineNotes.zh: c 从 b 的下一个数开始，理由和 b 从 a 的下一个数开始一样：不满足条件的组合根本不产生。

lineNotes.en: print always returns None, so a comprehension made of print calls is a list of Nones.
lineNotes.zh: print 总是返回 None，所以由 print 调用组成的推导式就是一串 None。
